summary.text: Matthew Simpson is the incumbent Republican and Conservative Party candidate for New York State Assembly District 114 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A former small business owner in the construction trades and onetime Horicon town supervisor, he was first elected to the Assembly in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Simpson grew up in the North Country and, before entering public service, was a small business owner for more than 30 years in the construction trades industry.

He won a seat on the Horicon Town Board in 2011, was elected Town Supervisor two years later, and served as supervisor until his election to the Assembly; as supervisor he also sat on the Warren County Board of Supervisors, where he chaired the Public Works and Personnel committees.
He was appointed to the Warren and Washington County IDA in 2015 and chaired it from 2018 to 2019, and he has served as president of the Adirondack Association of Towns and Villages.
Simpson was elected to the Assembly on November 3, 2020, and represents a district that includes Essex and Warren counties and parts of Saratoga, Washington and Fulton counties.
He is a member of the Environmental Conservation, Governmental Operations, Local Governments, Social Services, and Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development committees.
His official biography lists public safety, state parks, support for local businesses, government transparency and lower taxes among his priorities.
